title: Residency-aware materialized views and field-level redaction for analytics pipelines
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Background: As customers adopt Redwood Dedicated and Private deployments across regulated geographies, product telemetry and usage analytics must be replicated and stored in regionally compliant stores while minimizing cross-border data exposure. Current pipeline copies raw events to a central analytics cluster and then fans out derivatives to regional stores. That approach exposes PII and increases cross-region copies, causing compliance friction and cost.

Goal: Implement a residency-first pipeline that creates region-scoped materialized views at ingestion time with configurable field-level redaction and per-tenant residency policy enforcement. The system should produce lightweight region-native artifacts suitable for reporting and console dashboards without sending full raw events outside the tenant's allowed regions.

Scope and constraints:
- Apply residency rules per-tenant (tenant has allowed_regions list) and per-event type (usage, errors, traces).
- Support field-level redaction policies: mask, remove, hash, or tokenization; policies must be pluggable and key-managed.
- Materialized views should be incrementally maintained (append-only + compaction) and designed for fast reads for Console dashboards and billing jobs.
- Maintain ability to run cross-region read-only analytics for internal SRE/infra use via audited, ephemeral queries; not covered by this ticket beyond a design note.
- Minimize changes to producers; prefer ingestion-time transforms inside the pipeline (e.g., Kafka streams/Flink/Beam) or edge adapters in regional ingestion gateways.

Proposed design (high level):
1) Residency policy service: small config store (tenant -> allowed_regions + redaction profile) with API used by ingestion workers and console query layer.
2) Ingestion router: region-aware fronting layer routes raw events to the closest regional ingestion fleet. For tenants restricted to a single region, raw payload stays in that region only.
3) Transform & redact step: stream processor applies the tenant's redaction profile using a pluggable transform registry (mask/hash/tokenize). Tokenization uses a decorrelated token service backed by customer KMS keys when needed.
4) Region materialized views: for each target region, the pipeline writes a compressed columnar store (daily/rolling) optimized for the Console: pre-aggregates, per-route cost breakdown, and time-series. Views are schema-versioned and published to region-local object stores with metadata catalog entries.
5) Catalog & access controls: a metadata catalog with residency tags ensures Console reads only from allowed region artifacts. Console Query API enforces tenant residency at query time.
6) Rollout & fallback: when regional capacity missing or a transform fails, pipeline falls back to a minimal anonymized summary that can be exported cross-region for global billing while maintaining audit trail.

Acceptance criteria:
- Residency policy service implemented with CRUD API and unit tests.
- Stream transform implements mask/hash/tokenize + KMS-backed tokenization integration with test vectors.
- End-to-end test demonstrating ingestion of a tenant-configured single-region tenant: raw event never appears in non-authorized region object stores; materialized view produced and readable by Console.
- Console dashboards for cost/latency reflect data from region materialized views for tenant-scoped queries.
- Performance target: per-event transform adds <12ms p50 to ingestion path in common payload sizes; cost delta quantified.
- Migration plan documented with rollback steps and a canary plan for 5 pilot tenants.

Data migration / rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (canary): deploy residency service and transform to eu-west-1; choose 3 internal tenants + 2 pilot customers, monitor correctness.
- Phase 2: enable materialized view writes for additional regions + automated verification job comparing legacy central views to region views (sampling only).
- Phase 3: cutover for tenants with strict residency flags; provide an opt-in flag for other tenants.

Testing and observability:
- Add lineage logging for transformed fields; store ephemeral hashes for verification during audits (log entries have redact-safe markers).
- Metrics: per-tenant transform latency histogram, per-region materialized view lag, bytes reduced after redaction, number of cross-region copies avoided.
- Alerts: materialized view lag > 5 minutes for >5% of partitions, transform error rate >0.1% sustained.

Security & compliance notes:
- Tokenization keys tied to tenant KMS keys where available; fallback to platform-managed keys requires customer consent.
- Audit trail for any cross-region export must include approver user and timestamp and be surfaced in Console's compliance logs.
- Security review required before any pilot with real customer data.

Trade-offs and open questions:
- Option A (ingestion-side transforms) keeps raw events regional but requires runtime GPU/CPU capacity near edge. Option B (centralized transform) simplifies operator ops but increases cross-region raw copies. Chosen: Option A for residency-compliant tenants; central transforms retained for non-residency tenants.
- Field-level tokenization complexity vs. downstream analytics fidelity — need to define which consumer jobs can accept hashed/tokenized values.
- Storage format: Parquet vs. custom columnar store tuned for Console reads. Prototype in Parquet first.

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc (internal): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFR/Residency+Materialized+Views
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2741
- Compliance checklist: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-residency-checklist

Next steps (short-term):
- Finalize transform SDK surface and register tokenization adapter (owner: @Liam)
- Build residency policy service skeleton and CI mocks (owner: @Aisha)
- Create E2E test harness that can run in a multi-region dev staging environment (owner: @Sanjay)
acceptance_criteria: Residency policy CRUD API implemented and exercised by ingestion workers
Transform library supports mask, hash, tokenize; sample vectors validated
End-to-end demo with single-region tenant proving no cross-region raw copies
Console surfaces dashboards using region materialized views for tenant-scoped queries
Instrumentation: latency, lag, error rate metrics present and alerts configured
